evals.prompt: Map this entire codebase for me, it's a Node API at ~/work/billing-api.
evals.expected_output: The full pipeline run in order, producing all nine documents plus a stamped index in docs/codebase-map/, pausing between phases.
assertions: docs/codebase-map/ is created in the target repo
The tech stack is produced before the architecture map
Flows are traced after the static maps, not before
Diagrams and the onboarding guide are produced last
A README.md index is written that links every generated document
The index is stamped with the commit sha and the date
The run pauses between phases rather than emitting all nine documents at once

evals.prompt: document this repo so a new person can understand it
evals.expected_output: The full mapping pipeline with the index as the front door.
assertions: Multiple documents are produced under docs/codebase-map/
An index README.md links all of them
The onboarding guide is produced and identified as the starting point
No file outside docs/codebase-map/ is written

evals.prompt: Map the codebase but I only have 20 minutes, don't do the whole thing.
evals.expected_output: A reduced run that completes the static maps and the index rather than doing one document perfectly and skipping the rest.
assertions: The response completes the static maps and the index rather than a single deep document
Flows or diagrams are explicitly deferred rather than silently skipped
An index README.md is still produced
The response states what was left out so it can be run later
